en: Your U.P.I. app says eight hundred and forty rupees debited. But the shop's soundbox is silent, and you're both staring like it's a third umpire review.
Is your money gone? No. In three minutes — where it is right now, when it comes back, and the mistake that makes you pay twice.
Here's what happens after you type your pin.
Step one, your bank takes the money out. That's your debited message.
Step two, N.P.C.I. — the middleman that runs U.P.I. — calls the shop's bank: add this money.
Think about it — it's a phone call. And like every call in India... three things can happen.
One, the shop's bank picks up — done, the shop got it. That's success.
Two, it picks up — sorry, can't take it, maybe an account problem. That's failed.
Your money already left, so N.P.C.I. tells your bank to return it. Failed sounds scary, but it's final — the money comes back, so pay again.
Three, the troublemaker. N.P.C.I. calls... and the line goes quiet. Hello? Hello? Call dropped.
Did the shop's bank add the money before it dropped? Nobody knows. Your app shows this as pending, or processing.
No answer in fifteen seconds? N.P.C.I. doesn't cancel it. It keeps it on hold, and sorts it out later.
Here's the catch — that call is just a message. The actual money moves later, in bulk, ten times a day, through the R.B.I.
So where is your money? After the next batch, it's safe with the shop's bank. Only question — did it reach the shop?
Next day, the shop's bank checks its books like a teacher taking attendance. Two answers.
Yes, we gave it to the shop — so the shop has it, soundbox or not.
Or, no, we never did — then it comes back to you.
How long? Paid a person — by the next day. Paid a shop — within five days. That's the R.B.I. limit. Miss it, and the bank pays you one hundred rupees for every extra day, even if you don't complain.
Quick summary, the way I remember it. Success, the shop got it. Failed, pay again. Processing, wait — a day for a person, up to five days for a shop.
My one rule: never pay again while it says processing. If it was a yes, congrats — you paid double for one packet of biscuits.
Ask the shopkeeper to check their bank S.M.S., not the soundbox. Still stuck? In your app's history, tap that payment, then U.P.I. Help. Paid twice? Pick duplicate payment.
Send this to that friend who always pays twice — I know you have one.
